questions.q: Why does Bellhaven still need a real backup strategy once AG_Bellhaven exists?
options: An AG protects against server and site loss, but replicates corruption or bad deletes just as fast as good data — it isn't a substitute for backups
Availability Groups don't work unless a separate backup job runs first
Backups are only needed to initially create the Availability Group
They don't — an AG makes traditional backups unnecessary
questions.explain: An AG replicates whatever happens to the data, good or bad. Only real, restorable backups protect against logical damage like a bad delete.

questions.q: How often does BellhavenOLTP's log backup run, and why that specific interval?
options: Every 5 minutes, to match the business's stated 5-minute RPO directly
Every 24 hours, matching the full backup schedule
Once per week, since log backups are only for archival
There is no log backup schedule — only full and differential
questions.explain: A log backup bounds data loss directly, so the 5-minute interval was chosen to match the stated RPO exactly.

questions.q: Why is BellhavenOLTP's full backup marked WITH COPY_ONLY?
options: Because only COPY_ONLY full backups (along with log backups) are supported when the backup runs on a secondary replica in an Availability Group
COPY_ONLY is required for every full backup regardless of AG membership
COPY_ONLY backups run faster than normal full backups
COPY_ONLY disables compression
questions.explain: Secondary replicas in an AG only support COPY_ONLY full backups and log backups — a normal full backup that resets the differential base isn't supported there.

questions.q: Why must BellhavenOLTP's differential backup run on SQLPRD01 (the primary), not a secondary?
options: Differential backups aren't supported on secondary replicas at all — there's no way for a secondary to track the differential bitmap independently
Differential backups are always slower on a secondary
SQLPRD01 has faster disks than the other replicas
Secondary replicas cannot run any kind of backup
questions.explain: Differential backups require tracking changes since the last full, which only the primary can do — this is a real, deliberate AG limitation, not a performance choice.

questions.q: What does sys.fn_hadr_backup_is_preferred_replica do in the log backup job?
options: It lets the job check whether the local replica is the one the AG's backup preference designates, so only that replica actually performs the scheduled backup
It forces a failover if a backup fails
It automatically restores a log backup on another replica
It reports the current RPO in minutes
questions.explain: The function checks the local replica against AUTOMATED_BACKUP_PREFERENCE, letting the same job be deployed to every replica while only the correct one executes it.
